claims.text: Midgard faces a substantial loss in wheat import value from Orvan following the expiration of the corridor agreement, with monthly values dropping by more than half since the deal ended.

citations.quote: In December 2025, the value was USD 85.0M and the volume was 236,000 tonnes.
In December 2026, the value was USD 34.1M and the volume was 83,000 tonnes.

assumptions: The December 2025 value represents the standard 'corridor' flow.
Vanir substitutes are currently insufficient to bridge the gap.

exposure.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for the months of October, November, and December following the corridor expiry.
assumptions: Aggregate loss across the first full quarter post-expiry is the most robust measure of initial disruption impact.
missing_data: Precise USD value of Vanir wheat substitutes for Midgard in Q4 2026.
exposure.uncertainty_note: The high bound equals the low bound as it uses the same three-month aggregate calculation.

limitations: While December data is available, full Q4 substitution volumes from Vanir are not yet quantified in the trade tables.

claims.text: Midgard's maize imports from Orvan saw a delayed but sharp decline, with value in the final quarter of 2026 falling significantly below 2025 levels.

citations.quote: In December 2025, the value was USD 84.4M and the volume was 222,000 tonnes.
In December 2026, the value was USD 31.5M and the volume was 74,000 tonnes.
The October volume held up longer than the wheat routes because a share of the maize trade was on delayed delivery terms.

assumptions: Delayed delivery terms mitigated losses in October but ceased to provide cover by November/December.

exposure.metric_definition: Aggregate year-on-year change in import value from Orvan for Oct-Dec 2026 compared to Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: The three-month window captures the shift from delayed delivery support to the full impact of the corridor's end.
exposure.uncertainty_note: Data for Tolan maize is missing, so this estimate is restricted to Midgard.

limitations: Alternative maize sources are not specified in the current evidence.

claims.text: Tolan's wheat import exposure is high, with the value of shipments from Orvan in the fourth quarter of 2026 dropping by more than 50% compared to the same period in 2025.

citations.quote: In December 2025, the value was USD 37.8M and the volume was 108,000 tonnes.
In December 2026, the value was USD 15.0M and the volume was 38,000 tonnes.

assumptions: Harbour Review trade data (Tier 2) is accurate for the Tolan-Orvan route.

exposure.metric_definition: Total value loss for Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025 for Orvan to Tolan wheat.
assumptions: Year-on-year quarterly comparison is the standard metric for identifying disruption impact.
missing_data: Vanir wheat shipment values to Tolan.
exposure.uncertainty_note: Based on Tier 2 trade notes; Tier 1 data for this specific pair is not available.

limitations: Specific Vanir substitute values for Tolan are noted as 'small' but not quantified in USD.

claims.text: Midgard's exposure to the expiration of the Orvan corridor for wheat was mitigated by a significant increase in shipments from Vanir, which reached Midgard in larger volumes starting in November 2026.

citations.quote: Vanir wheat reached Midgard in larger volumes from November, mostly on short-term contracts.
In November 2026, the value was USD 38.5M and the volume was 96,000 tonnes.
On these assumptions, the net value loss for Midgard wheat is close to 40%, once Vanir supply is included.

assumptions: Vanir production and logistics can maintain the increased volume levels through January 2027.
Short-term contracts mentioned in ORV-0027 are renewable or represent a stable shift in trade.

exposure.metric_definition: The year-over-year change in import value from Orvan for the first full quarter after the agreement expiration (Oct-Dec), representing the gross trade gap.
assumptions: The gross import gap is the primary driver of exposure before accounting for higher-priced substitutes.
missing_data: Precise January 2027 delivery figures from Vanir to confirm the low-end estimate.
exposure.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -156.5..-156.5 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 156.5..156.5] The estimate reflects the gross value gap; net exposure is lower due to documented Vanir increases.

limitations: The sea route remains the cheapest bulk transport option, making substitutes like Vanir wheat likely more expensive per tonne.
Vanir's small base limit's its total offset capacity.

claims.text: Midgard's maize imports from Orvan showed high resilience immediately following the corridor expiration due to delayed delivery terms, which buffered the initial shock.

citations.quote: The October volume held up longer than the wheat routes because a share of the maize trade was on delayed delivery terms.
In October 2026, the value was USD 62.1M and the volume was 146,000 tonnes.

assumptions: Delayed delivery terms provided an inventory cushion that Midgard utilized to source alternatives or adjust demand.

exposure.metric_definition: The year-over-year change in Orvan maize import value for Oct-Dec 2026 versus Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: Year-over-year comparison accounts for seasonal variance in maize trade.
missing_data: Maize inventory levels in Midgard as of January 2027.
exposure.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -126.4..-126.4 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 126.4..126.4] The 'low' exposure is supported by the delayed volume in October which was nearly 75% of the prior year's level.

limitations: Delayed delivery terms only postpone the impact and do not solve the long-term supply deficit.

claims.text: Tolan's wheat exposure was partially offset by increased shipments from Vanir, mirroring the trend seen in Midgard.

citations.quote: Vanir has increased wheat shipments to Tolan and Midgard.
In November 2026, the value was USD 26.5M and the volume was 67,000 tonnes.
Tolan buyers replaced part of the lost volume with wheat from Vanir

assumptions: The upward trend in Vanir-to-Tolan shipments continued into January 2027.

exposure.metric_definition: The year-over-year change in Orvan wheat import value for Oct-Dec 2026 versus Oct-Dec 2025.
assumptions: The gap in Orvan sea trade is the maximum exposure before considering Vanir's offset.
missing_data: Quantitative data for Ravik rail movements to Tolan which are known to be 'high'.
exposure.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -69.6..-69.6 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 69.6..69.6] Tolan's actual exposure is likely lower than this gross value due to the 'high' rail loadings through Ravik.

limitations: The replacement volume from Vanir was noted to be smaller than the total gap left by Orvan.

claims.text: Exposure for Tolan maize imports cannot be quantified due to a lack of monthly trade data, though rail routes remain an active alternative.

citations.quote: Rail loadings through Ravik remain high
the deal covered wheat and maize leaving the port by sea; it did not cover rail movements

assumptions: Rail infrastructure through Ravik is capable of handling maize as well as wheat.
limitations: There is a complete absence of monthly trade volume and value for Orvan to Tolan maize imports (2025-2026) in the available records.
